The C2 aGVHD estimate (OR 0.63, k = 8) is too small for formal bias assessment but remains consistent. ### CMV Reactivation ::: {#tbl-grade-cmv .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — CMV.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~C1, ~C2, "Study design", "1 RCT + 21 retro; start LOW", "All retrospective; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "0 (monitoring protocol heterogeneity noted)", "0 (direction uncertain)", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 62%)", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 71%)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (CrI excludes null [1.07\u20131.47])", "\u22121 (CrI crosses null [0.73\u20131.15])", "Upgrade", "+1 (steroid-independence; sensitivity convergence pattern)", "0 (see below)", "Net", "0", "\u22122", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## CMV: From Direction Reversal to Depletion Gradient The pre-Block-9 analysis reported a qualitative direction reversal: PTCy increased CMV vs CNI+MTX (OR 1.41) but decreased it vs ATG (OR 0.77 [0.60–0.99]). In the post-Block-9 corpus, C2 CMV has shifted to OR 0.97 [0.77–1.23], and the CrI crosses null. The binary reversal is no longer statistically credible. However, the **C2 sensitivity analysis** provides a different — and arguably stronger — form of evidence. When PTCy+ATG combination arms are reclassified as "PTCy-side" (k = 22), the CMV estimate converges to OR 1.00 [0.85–1.18]. This convergence is predicted by the depletion hierarchy: when both arms have deep T-cell depletion, CMV rates should equalise. The three estimates trace a gradient: | Analysis | Arms compared | OR | Interpretation | |---|---|---|---| | C1 primary | PTCy vs CNI | 1.26 | PTCy depletes more → more CMV | | C2 primary | PTCy vs ATG | 0.97 | Near-parity; slight PTCy advantage | | C2 sensitivity | PTCy+ATG vs ATG | 1.00 | Equal depletion → equal CMV | This gradient is more consistent with the depletion hierarchy than the pre-Block-9 binary reversal. The mechanistic conclusion — that CMV risk tracks T-cell depletion depth, not any PTCy-specific property — carries **LOW certainty** when assessed across the full evidence pattern, despite the individual C2 estimate being VERY LOW. ::: ### BSI and IFI ::: {#tbl-grade-infection .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — BSI and IFI.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~`C1 BSI`, ~`C1 IFI`, "Study design", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "\u22121 (definitions heterogeneous)", "0", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 71%; freq CrI crosses null)", "\u22121 (\u03c4 = 1.64; I\u00B2 = 80%)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (Bayes CrI excludes null)", "0 (CrI excludes null [0.29\u20130.63])", "Net", "\u22122", "\u22121", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

The Bayesian shrinkage prior and the frequentist random-effects model disagree, reducing confidence. IFI: The post-Block-9 estimate (OR 0.43 [0.29–0.63]) is substantially stronger than pre-Block-9 (0.73 [0.53–1.00]), but τ = 1.64 indicates extreme between-study heterogeneity. The frequentist CrI (0.21–1.74) again crosses null. With only k = 6 studies and this level of heterogeneity, the strong protective signal should be interpreted cautiously. ::: {.callout-warning} ## Publication-bias analyses are pre-deduplication The Egger, trim-and-fill and RoBMA results in this section were computed before the Set B cohort deduplication and have not been regenerated. They should be read as indicative only; the C1 OS funnel in particular included five EBMT ALWP publications that are now represented by one. ::: ## Publication Bias {#sec-grade-pubbias} Formal assessment was conducted for C1 outcomes with k ≥ 10 using Egger's regression test and trim-and-fill. ::: {#tbl-grade-pubbias .cell tbl-cap='Publication bias assessment — C1 outcomes with k ≥ 10.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Outcome, ~k, ~`Egger z`, ~`Egger p`, ~`T&F imputed`, ~`Original OR`, ~`Adjusted OR`, "OS", 40, -1.02, 0.314, 7, "0.77 [0.66\u20130.90]", "0.86 [0.73\u20131.02]", "aGVHD", 28, -2.15, 0.041, 8, "0.61 [0.47\u20130.79]", "0.83 [0.61\u20131.13]", "CMV", 22, -0.21, 0.835, 0, "1.25 [0.94\u20131.66]", "1.25 [0.94\u20131.66]" ) |> mutate(`Egger p` = ifelse(`Egger p` < 0.05, paste0("**", sprintf("%.3f", `Egger p`), "**"), sprintf("%.3f", `Egger p`))) |> kable(align = c("l","r","r","r","r","c","c")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Outcome k Egger z Egger p T&F imputed Original OR Adjusted OR
OS 40 -1.02 0.314 7 0.77 [0.66–0.90] 0.86 [0.73–1.02]
aGVHD 28 -2.15 **0.041** 8 0.61 [0.47–0.79] 0.83 [0.61–1.13]
CMV 22 -0.21 0.835 0 1.25 [0.94–1.66] 1.25 [0.94–1.66]
````` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## C1 aGVHD: Significant Funnel Asymmetry Egger's test detects significant small-study bias (p = 0.041). After trim-and-fill imputation, the adjusted OR shifts from 0.61 to 0.83 and the CI crosses null. The Bayesian pooled estimate (OR 0.67 [0.59–0.78]) is less extreme than the frequentist 0.61, reflecting shrinkage, but does not account for selective non-publication. C1 aGVHD certainty is downgraded from LOW to VERY LOW. C1 OS shows borderline concern: 7 studies imputed with adjusted OR touching null (0.86 [0.73–1.02]), though Egger's test is non-significant (p = 0.31). C1 CMV is symmetric with no imputed studies. ::: ## Narrative Summary {#sec-grade-narrative} Across both comparisons, certainty does not exceed LOW — a predictable consequence of an almost entirely observational evidence base. **The most robust findings** are C1 OS (OR 0.84, k = 35, LOW certainty) and C1 moderate-severe cGVHD (OR 0.47, k = 19, LOW certainty). Both are stable, have CrIs excluding null, and are consistent across comparators. C1 cGVHD is the largest treatment effect in the analysis. C1 RRM (OR 0.86, k = 34, LOW certainty) is similarly robust and steroid-independent, supporting preserved GVL activity. **Cross-comparison coherence** remains the strongest methodological asset. **Chronic GVHD is arguably the most clinically important finding.** The OR of 0.33 for moderate-severe cGVHD translates to a two-thirds reduction in the leading cause of late post-transplant morbidity. Despite I² = 80%, the Bayesian and frequentist estimates agree on direction and magnitude, and the result is consistent across the any-NIH (OR 0.23) and moderate-severe (OR 0.33) subsets. **The infection–mortality disconnect is the key risk-benefit finding.** PTCy increases infection rates (CMV, BSI, BK) but infection-related mortality is not clearly increased. The C1 IRM Bayesian–frequentist divergence (OR 1.35 vs 1.01) warrants caution, but even the more pessimistic estimate represents a far smaller effect than the infection rate increases, suggesting infectious complications are clinically manageable. **C2 NRM is no longer gradeable.** Arm classification corrections reduced k to 3. NRM steroid mediation is inconclusive in the post-Block-9 data. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Post-Block-9 GRADE Changes - **New outcomes added:** cGVHD moderate-severe (C1 LOW, C2 V.LOW), RRM (C1 LOW, C2 LOW), BK virus (V.LOW), IRM (V.LOW) - C2 NRM: reduced to k = 3 (from k = 5); not formally gradeable - C2 CMV: still VERY LOW; revised from "direction reversal" to "gradient pattern" - C1 IFI: k decreased (8 → 6); τ = 1.64 warrants extreme caution - C1 IRM: Bayesian–frequentist divergence; rated VERY LOW - C1 NRM mediation: no longer shows clear complete mediation (M1→M2 shift minimal) :::
